roleTitle: Model Evaluation Engineer, Wealth Services Platform
jobDescription: The wealth services platform of a private bank uses models to flag unusual portfolio movements for adviser review. The Model Evaluation Engineer maintains the evaluation harness and the labelled review set, runs pre-release evaluations for each model version, and is expected to reduce the false-alert rate seen by advisers, reported against the platform's documented quarterly baseline.
requirements: Maintains the model evaluation harness and the labelled adviser-review set.
Runs pre-release evaluations for each model version and publishes the evaluation report.
Reduces the false-alert rate seen by advisers, reported against the documented quarterly baseline.
Coordinates release decisions with the model team and adviser operations and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents evaluation assumptions, known limitations and hand-over conditions for each model version.

evidence.text: Maintained the evaluation harness (Python, scheduled on the platform's batch runner) and the labelled review set of adviser-confirmed alerts, adding 1,200 newly labelled alerts over the year.
Ran the pre-release evaluation for each of the four model versions released in the year and published the evaluation report to the model team and adviser operations.

The false-alert rate seen by advisers fell from 31 percent in Q1 to 18 percent in Q4 after the threshold recalibration I proposed was adopted in version 3.2, as measured on the labelled review set and reported against the documented Q1 baseline of 31 percent.
Coordinated release decisions in the model release meeting; the model team lead took the go/no-go decision and adviser operations confirmed the alert-volume impact.

Wrote the evaluation notes for each version, listing the review-set composition, the known limitation that alerts on newly onboarded portfolios were under-represented, and the hand-over items for the next evaluation.

Work sample: the quarterly false-alert report (rate per quarter, baseline line, version 3.2 marker) and the evaluation notes for version 3.2, with the batch runner's job identifiers as a verification trail.

Reference call with former model team lead: confirmed the false-alert figures come from the quarterly evaluation report on the labelled set, that the threshold recalibration was the candidate's proposal, and the employment dates.
Recruiter logistics note: candidate can present the evaluation harness in a technical session next week.

gold.expectedGap: Hand-over conditions for each model version are only partly documented in the evaluation notes.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the false-alert result as stated for the labelled review set and the year; do not extend it to alert precision in general.
